answer.evidence: The column at x=24 shows a gray coping band on rows 17-19 with a darker front-edge line at row 20. Dark brown eave shadow follows on rows 21-22, and the red brick front face runs from row 21 to 31 (about 11 rows). The east pier has its own light gray cap on rows 12-16 above a brick face. The main wall therefore reads as three-quarter, with a 4-row coping top over a tall brick front. The crumbled west half is drawn only as a broken brick face with jagged tops and no visible horizontal surface, so not every major part has a top.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small wall prop set against two full houses, so I judged structure and shading craft rather than size. Measured facts are at or above both references: 15 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10, 0% near-flat coverage like both references, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, which means the edges carry a tint. The outline reads as dark red-brown beside the brick and dark brown at the base, not black. The brick courses show a few tones (light coping, mid and dark red-brown, shadow), with loose bricks and small green or yellow bits on the ground. That is close to the Beodeul brick and tile treatment, with per-brick variation and no big flat fills. Shading is a little shallower than the roof ramps in the references (about 5 steps against 5-6), and the piece is tiny, so fine texture is hard to read at this scale. I see no sticker-style black outline and nothing plainly thinner or flatter than the references.
